title: Bird elevation centroids on fixed survey routes moved under 10 m upslope as isotherms rose about 160 m in US and Swedish mountain blocks; elevation tracking was not better than latitude tracking
abstract: Question: do bird species follow warming better along elevation, where full tracking needs only about 160 m, than along latitude, where it needs 170-260 km? Data: Breeding Bird Survey standard runs on fixed contiguous-US routes (1975-1989 versus 2010-2024) and Swedish Bird Survey fixed routes (1998-2007 versus 2016-2025, CC0), ETOPO1 route elevation, nClimGrid and E-OBS temperature. Method (pre-registered): in mountain blocks (4 or more routes, elevation range 300 m or more), abundance-weighted elevation centroids per species and block; comparison with the isotherm shift (warming divided by local lapse rate) and with latitude shifts on the same routes; raw counts and route-normalised shares; block bootstrap and within-route permutation. Post hoc, we calibrated the shift that full tracking gives on the fixed routes. Results: warming of 0.86-0.94 C raised isotherms 163-165 m. Mean species elevation shifts were +1.4 m (US West, CI -7.2 to 14.1; 287 species), -0.5 m (US East, -4.4 to 5.9; 232 species) and +6.4 m (Sweden, -0.5 to 11.5; 157 species). Full tracking would move the route centroids 69, 17 and 22 m. Pooled calibrated elevation tracking was 0.05 (-0.06 to 0.23) on raw counts and 0.01 (-0.08 to 0.17) on shares; latitude tracking was 0.22 and 0.12. No region met the pre-registered rule for better elevation tracking; in a 1995-2004 versus 2015-2024 US window latitude tracking was larger (difference -0.33, CI -0.65 to -0.09). The all-bird centroid moved 5-13 m upslope, so route-level count changes are as large as the species signal. Sweden showed a repeated small upslope shift (3-8 m) whose calibrated size depends on the smoothing bandwidth. Conclusion: a short distance to a cooler climate did not make birds track warming better. Limitations: two-period correlational design, no detection model, road-based routes, 25-km Swedish coordinates, post hoc calibration.
